COMMON GROUND — ALL FOUR BOARDS, THE MOTOR PACK AND EVERY COMPONENT
One star point. Motor return and logic return meet there and nowhere else. Full distribution on SCHEMA_POWER.svg.
1. Only P3_27 / P3_28 are 5 V tolerant on the MCX. Both Arduino TX lines reach it through
a 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ divider; the two MCX TX lines are plain wire (3.3 V clears the AVR's 3.0 V).
2. TX and RX cross. An MCX TX pin always lands on an Arduino D4. Never TX to TX.
3. Power the HC-SR04P from the Arduino's 5 V. It is on a 5 V node, so the P variant's
3.3–5 V range buys you nothing here — it matters only if you ever move it to the MCX.
4. Two separate I²C buses. LPI2C0 is 3.3 V (ESP32 + IMU). The LCD is on ACT's own 5 V bus.
Joining them puts 5 V pull-ups on P3_27 / P3_28 and kills the MCX.
5. MG90S servos draw far more than an Arduino pin header can supply — V+ comes from the
battery pack, signal from D6 / D7, grounds common. See the power sheet.
6. Servo library on PERC owns Timer1. Motor PWM on ACT owns Timer1. That is why they are
on different boards — one Uno cannot do both.
7. ESP32 GPIO6–11 are wired to its flash and must stay unused. GPIO34–39 are input-only,
which is exactly what the camera data lines need. GPIO0 is a strapping pin: if the
camera holds it low at boot the ESP32 will not start — unplug the camera to flash.
8. D0 / D1 stay free on both Arduinos — shared with the CH340 bootloader.
9. Wheels off the floor for every reset until the 10 kΩ pull-downs are on ENA / ENB.
10. The ESP32's native CAN is real but unusable here: TWAI still needs a transceiver, and
the MCX has no CAN peripheral at all. Two of four nodes could never join the bus.
